context: The party is in a crypt before a richly adorned sarcophagus; several of Jergal’s skeletal clerics (his servants) are still active and have not been slain. The player has just touched the sarcophagus, prompting Jergal to reproach them—telling them to deal with the dead first—rather than allow them to disturb him. Jergal is the emotionless, excessively formal judge of death who was sealed inside by the god Helm as penance for his role in raising the Dead Three; he is functionally immortal and bound to assist the party. He offers help (including resurrection services) only because of that divine oath, not personal goodwill, and attempts to anger or attack him have little effect; his immediate aim is merely to see the party’s faces and later find them in camp.
